subject: Quadrant Health: perf qualification recap & pack request
thread_body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@quadranthealth.com>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@quadranthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Sep 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quadrant Health: perf qualification recap & pack request

Hi Samira / Ethan —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the ask list so we can get your perf qualification started next week: 

1) Targets and workload slice we heard today
   - 95th latency SLO target: 120ms (token-level tail) for sync generation path
   - Avg throughput target: 1,200 concurrent QPS across your shard (expected burst to 3k qps)
   - Streaming: per-connection latency (time-to-first-payload) goal 40ms and sustained streaming throughput for multi-turn sessions
   - Max concurrent KV-cache-enabled sessions: ~800 per region

2) Deliverables Redwood will provide before the run
   - Benchmark harness access (read-only) + run recipe
   - Canonical prompt set (sample attached) and prompt bucketing guidance
   - Measurement definitions (latency percentiles, cold vs warm, concurrency model) and reproducibility notes

3) What we need from Quadrant Health
   - Production-like prompt samples and a short traffic mix (attached example: quadrant_prompt_sample.jsonl)
   - Network traces or aggregated egress latency histograms (optional but very helpful)
   - A contact for on-call during run windows (Ethan offered to be on standby)

Next steps
- I’ll drop a short mutual action plan PDF into Drive and HubSpot.
- Ben will send the eval harness invite and a short run checklist.
- Kimberly to share the measurement spec and a reproducibility checklist.

If that matches your notes, reply with any missing pieces and we’ll schedule the first reproducible run for Tue 09/12 10:00 PT (we can shift if you prefer).

Thanks —
Priyom
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments referenced: quadrant_prompt_sample.jsonl (sample prompts), network_latency_trace_agg.csv (optional)

----------------------------------------------------------------
From: Samira Patel <samira@quadranthealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@quadranthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Sep 2028 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quadrant Health: perf qualification recap & pack request

Thanks Priyom — this is perfect and aligned. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 1,200 concurrent QPS number is our average expected across a single US region; our prod peak historically hits ~2.6k for short bursts. We want the validation to include a 20-minute soak at 2.6k burst to exercise autoscaling/fallbacks.
- For streaming, our sessions are typically 8–12 turns with short user pauses (200–600ms). We care most about time-to-first-payload for UX.

We’ll upload an anonymized prompt dump (PHI removed) by EOD today and attach an aggregated latency CSV. Ethan will be the run lead.

Samira
Head of Platform Engineering | Quadrant Health

----------------------------------------------------------------
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@quadranthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Sep 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quadrant Health: perf qualification recap & pack request

Looping in the harness and ops details so we can keep the customer looped. Priyom and I aligned offline on the run scope; suggested run window Tue 09/12 10:00 PT + a contingency Wed 09/13 morning if we need replay.

Key measurement notes for the harness (high level):
- Warm vs cold separation: 5-minute warmup, then 30-minute steady-state measurement; repeat for burst scenario (20-minute burst at peak qps).
- Latency buckets we publish: p50/p90/p95/p99 (per-token) and time-to-first-payload (for streaming).
- Concurrency: emulate KV-cache affinity groups to reflect session stickiness; use 60/30/10 bucket for short/medium/long sessions by token length.

I’ve added the mutual_action_plan_QH.pdf to Drive and HubSpot (link below). I’ll invite the Quadrant eng alias to the harness project with read/run rights.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

----------------------------------------------------------------
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@quadranthealth.com>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@quadranthealth.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2028 10:13:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: measurement spec draft + reproducibility checklist (please review)

Ben / Kimberly —

Posting a short internal note for the run. Please review the attached measurement spec and the reproducibility checklist I drafted. Key open items:
- Cold-start definition: do we need a strict per-worker cold window vs per-model? I lean per-worker (practical for their infra), but note will affect p99.
- Network conditioning: Samira offered aggregated traces; should we replay or use synthetic network shaping? My suggestion: replay aggregated histograms for US region then a synthetic 50ms jitter scenario for worst case.
- Prompt canonization: Kimberly, can you confirm we need the token-normalized variants (strip person names + normalize timestamps) or keep raw sanitized text? The customer removed PHI; normalization will improve reproducibility.

Action items assigned:
- Kimberly: finalize measurement spec + prompt canonization rules (target EOD 9/13).
- Ben: create harness run recipe and invite Quadrant alias.
- Priyom: coordinate run schedule and collect artifacts (prompts + traces).

Thanks — Priyom

----------------------------------------------------------------
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@quadranthealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@quadranthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quadrant Health: perf qualification recap & pack request

Samira / Ethan —

Attached is the measurement_spec_QH.md (pushed to Drive link below) and a short reproducibility checklist. Highlights: 

- Cold-start policy: we’ll use per-worker cold windows (60s idle) and mark those tokens separately. We’ll publish both combined and warm-only charts so you can see impact.
- Prompt canonization: we will use token-normalized variants as our canonical set (remove timestamps, replace high-entropy IDs with placeholders). We’ll retain a mapping file so you can replay raw sanitized prompts if needed.
- Repro checklist: exactly the harness git commit hash, seed, run recipe, and the dataset object (we generate immutable dataset IDs). We’ll include a small script to re-run the same harness locally for you.

I’ve invited the Quadrant Health Eng Team to the eval harness and uploaded the measurement_spec_QH.md and reproducibility_checklist.md to the Drive folder. Links: https://eval.redwood.ai/runs/QH-2028-0091-harness and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2Bq-QuadrantPerfPack

If you’re happy with the approach we’ll proceed with the 9/12 run as scheduled; otherwise say so and we’ll adjust.

Kimberly Park
Measurement Lead | Redwood Inference

Files added to Drive: measurement_spec_QH.md, reproducibility_checklist.md, mutual_action_plan_QH.pdf
